name: Praxiteles the Sculptor
bio: Praxiteles of Athens, the greatest sculptor of the fourth century BC, made the Cnidian Aphrodite and the Eros of Thespiae. The Anthology ascribes to him a poem spoken in the person of his own Eros; the attribution is a literary fiction.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the fifth volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Loeb, 1918): Book XVI: 204.

poems.title: Book XVI, 204: On the Same
poems.author: Praxiteles the Sculptor
poems.text: Praxiteles perfectly portrayed that Love he suffered, taking the model from his own heart, giving me to Phryne in payment for myself. But I give birth to passion no longer by shooting arrows, but by darting glances.
